analysis.title: Whack-a-mole Credit
key_insights: Credit spreads sold off about 70bps over the last month after sequential hits from technicals (hyperscaler oversupply in July), rates volatility (September) and AI-valuation sentiment (October). Each episode raised the baseline spread investors demand.
Most of the spread weakness comes from repricing of the AI complex and volatility premiums. Broad fundamental impact on LevFin issuers from the macro backdrop remains contained.

BofA says spread retracement depends on lower rates volatility and good Q3 earnings. Early read-throughs on both are good, but HY yield stays at 8.2% because markets focus on what-ifs (AI monetization collapsing, profitability not broadening beyond the AI complex).

HY NTM par default rate forecast is 2.5% vs 1.7% today. NTM issuer default rate forecast is 3.3% vs 3.0% currently. Drivers are near-term maturity walls at higher borrowing costs and a rising distress ratio.

The HY Credit Stress Indicator (CSI) rose from 26% to 47% YTD. It explains 65% of variation in the NTM par default rate and currently implies a 2.1% default rate. BofA expects defaults to exceed that.

8% of the HY index matures within 2 years and 24% within 3 years, both near historical highs. The HY distress ratio (share of index at OAS above 1,000bps) is 7% and has a 75% historical correlation with default rates.
Bottom-up HY analysis by rating and maturity gives an aggregate par default rate of 2.3%-2.5%, consistent with the 2.5% base case.
Loan NTM issuer and par default rate forecasts are 3.9% and 4.0%, vs current 2.4% issuer and 1.9% par. Loan defaults fell YTD but BofA expects a reversal.

Reasons for the loan default reversal: near-term maturity wall at 7.5% of the index and 19.6% of B3/CCC (highest since 2013), distress and shadow distress ratios up to 9.4% and 14.6%, and the Fed returning to a rate-hiking stance, which should raise LME activity.

Defaults may shift from 'bad capital structure, good business model' (the 2025 rate-led cycle) to 'decent capital structure, bad business model' from AI-led disintermediation. That could raise the share of hard defaults vs LMEs.

HY recovery forecast for 2027 is 32pt vs 34pt YTD. YTD 2026 recovery of 34pt missed BofA's 45pt forecast, with LMEs at 54pt vs hard defaults at 26pt and LMEs only 30% of defaulted par (42% in 2025). Downside case is 30pt, upside 40pt.

Loan first-lien recovery forecast for 2027 is 49pt vs 54pt YTD. The LME share of defaulted par is expected to fall from 77% to 55%, HD recovery from 49pt to 40pt, with a sector mix shifting to asset-light software and services. Downside case is 47pt, upside 52pt.
27% of software and services debt is due in 2027-2029 vs 20% for all other sectors, which exposes it to AI disruption risk.

The 2026 HY hard-default cohort was concentrated in retail, packaging and chemicals, not the AI-exposed sectors BofA flagged in March. AI-related pressures could still raise the HD share and lower recoveries in 2027.
AI-related USD credit issuance is $581bn YTD: $259bn IG, $53bn HY, $16bn institutional loans, $252bn private credit/direct lending/bilateral. Issuance was unchanged on the week.
IG AI-related bonds trade at 140bps vs 75bps for comparable ex-AI bonds, a record 65bps premium. The prior YTD wide was 131bps on Jul 29.
HY AI-related bonds hit a record 400bps (+23bps WTD) vs 209bps ex-AI, a 191bps premium, above the early September wide of 178bps. Data excludes CRWV.
HY spreads closed at 327bps, broadly unchanged WoW. CCC spreads widened 25bps WoW and 230bps MTD. HY total return was +15bps WoW and -10bps MTD. CCCs returned -225bps MTD, BBs +25bps MTD.

HY funds saw a third straight week of outflows, cumulative $2.4bn, with $0.5bn WTD. HY primary issuance was $1.7bn with no refinancings. Internal demand was $4.1bn this week and slows to $2.7bn of calls/maturities plus $0.9bn of coupons next week.
HY CSI is 46.8%, up 5.1% WoW, and Loan CSI is 55.7%, up 2.0% WoW. Net HY downgrades were $2.8bn for the fourth straight week, with the notional shrinking each week.
USD loan index returned -0.10% WTD (price -0.18pt to 94.5). CCC loans -0.52% WTD and -8.91% YTD. Loans are +2.88% YTD, with BB loans at +4.04%.
Loan fund flows: CLO ETFs +$20.0bn YTD, BSL open-ends -$4.5bn YTD. YTD loan demand net of supply is +$89.5bn vs +$70.7bn a year ago. Loan new issuance was $6.57bn over seven days, 68.1% for LBOs.

Sector moves: HY Chemicals (-135bps) and Telecoms (-110bps) lagged on the week, while Financials, Transports (+70bps each) and Cap Goods (+55bps) led. Among loans, Cable (-454bps MTD) and Real Estate (-128bps MTD) were weak.
JetBlue's term loan fell 12.3pts to 52.2, which BofA tied to Bloomberg reports of heavy debt and rising oil prices. Artera Services fell 9.6pts and Cloudera 8.6pts.

market_movers.rationale: JetBlue term loan fell 12.3pts to 52.2 in the week, amid reports of heavy debt burden and rising oil prices.
CoreWeave screens rich to its CSI-implied OAS (OAS 989 vs OASe 748) and appears on the downgrade candidates list (B1, -3 notches projected).
Charter screens cheap to fair value (OAS 296 vs CSI-implied 584), but also appears on the downgrade candidates list.
Whirlpool screens cheap on the rich/cheap screen (OAS 619 vs OASe 809), though it is also a downgrade candidate (-3 notches).
Oracle is on the fallen angel watchlist (BBB2, $119bn face, OAS 276).
Hertz was downgraded one notch to CCC3 and appears on the default candidates list (price 50, CSI 0.987).
Caesars Entertainment was downgraded one notch to CCC1 in the recent downgrades list.
Live Nation is a rising star candidate (BB2, OAS 138) and priced a $730mn HY deal on 10/7.
United Rentals was upgraded one notch to BB1 and is also a rising star candidate.
Carvana was upgraded one notch to BB2.
Wayfair was upgraded one notch to BB2.
Electronic Arts appears on the upgrade candidates list (B3, +3 notches projected) and became a fallen angel in 08/26.

sector_views.rationale: BofA keeps a generally constructive view of credit but expects credit losses to rise from here, with defaults up and recoveries down in 2027.
Asset-light software and services carry a disproportionate share of near-term maturities and the most exposure to AI disruption, which weighs on expected loan recoveries.
AI-related spreads are at record premiums to ex-AI in both IG and HY, reflecting sentiment-driven repricing of the AI complex.

earnings_insights: BofA says good Q3 earnings are a precondition for spread retracement, and that momentum for AI-adjacent issuers is positive per its Earnings Tracker: Week 1. No specific company EPS or revenue figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Broadly unchanged WoW, +61bps over one month, with CCC spreads at 1,307bps.
Yields stay elevated even as treasuries come off their lows, due to negative sentiment.
Up from 1.7% today, driven by maturity walls and distress.
Up from 2.4% currently, as the YTD decline reverses.
Below 34pt YTD and the 45pt 2026 forecast, on fewer LMEs and weaker per-type recoveries.
Below 54pt YTD, with the default mix shifting toward hard defaults.
Share of the index trading at OAS above 1,000bps. Historically 75% correlated with default rates.
Higher rates raise interest burden and should increase LME activity.

risk_factors: Further repricing of the AI complex, with monetization collapsing or profitability not broadening beyond AI.
Elevated near-term maturity walls at higher borrowing costs, especially for CCC issuers and in loans (7.5% of the index due within 2 years).
Rising distress ratios (7% HY, 9.4% loan distress, 14.6% loan shadow distress).
The Fed returning to a rate-hiking stance, which raises interest burden and LME activity.
A faster or deeper AI disruption of asset-light software and services issuers, which would push loan recoveries toward the 47pt downside.
A rising share of hard defaults vs LMEs, which would lower recoveries.
High issuer-level dispersion makes headline recovery numbers less meaningful.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 earnings read-throughs are good and AI-adjacent issuer momentum is positive. Treasuries are off their lows and rates vol is easing, which BofA calls preconditions for spreads to retrace. Fundamental impact on LevFin is contained.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets are focused on what-ifs (AI monetization collapsing, profitability not broadening). HY yield stays at 8.2%, and defaults are expected to rise with a build in maturity walls and distress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued high rates volatility and failure of AI monetization to broaden beyond the AI complex, which would keep spreads from retracing.

tension_points.bull_case: Loan default rates fell YTD (par 3.2% to 1.9%) as issuers addressed maturity walls and LME activity fell with Fed cuts.
tension_points.bear_case: Maturity walls, distress ratios and the Fed rate-hiking stance all reversed, so BofA forecasts 3.9% issuer and 4.0% par default rates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed pivot away from hiking, or a sharp fall in the distress and shadow distress ratios from 9.4% and 14.6%.
